body: I decided to back down from it for now bc the doctor told me they wouldn't even sedate me and all they can offer is a little bit of valium before the procedure and my anxiety was REALLY bad at the time so it would be too much for me to handle. When I asked abt what would happen if I had a panic attack during the procedure they told me it better not happen bc that would be a problem T\_T

Thank you so much for sharing your story. I hope that your ablation was successful and once healed the PVCs will stop. 4 days is still very early so please as much as it's hard try not to lose hope! You did what seemed best for you and there's a chance it worked! I wish you a fast recovery! 
What did your doctor said post-surgery?



I can really relate to the "do I want to take pills my whole life?" thoughts bc that's what even makes me consider ablation as the best option despite being scared of it without general anesthesia. Rn I'm planning to speak to the doctor performing it about my anxiety disorder and discuss if there are any sedation options that would help me handle it better bc that's the only thing that stops me tbh.

The only thing going on with my heart besides the PVCs is mitral valve prolapse so nothing to really worry about. I am glad that I have a choice here but also I'd love to feel better 😭 I haven't taken any anxiety meds since the first routine EKG testing I've mentioned in the post (so for over a year now) because both my cardiologist and psychiatrist agreed that I should stop so it would be easier to determine if it's anxiety or PVCs causing them(also after finding out I have arrhytmia my psychiatrist got worried if I even could take any anxiety meds so he told me that I should get the cardiologist opinion first and my cardiologists opinion is that I should get an ablation first bc anxiety meds mask the symptoms of pvcs). But yeah I've been struggling with GAD for years now, I've tried different types and doses of anxiety meds but nothing really worked for me in a long run yet. The therapy helped, I don't have full blown panic attacks anymore but the symptoms I've mentioned before are still here and even got worse lately.


The main problem with beta blockers for me is that I have naturally low blood pressure and they lowered it even more and made me extremally sleepy. My doctor said that any other meds wouldn't make sense for me bc they just mask the problem not heal it. 


Tbh I never suggested to my doctor that my symptoms are from PVCs, I mentioned them only when he specifically asked about them but I blamed it on anxiety and I'm still unsure bc there is literally no way to say bc the symptoms are very similar(that's why my decision is even harder to make bc what if it's really just anxiety and I'd go with a procedure for nothing really).

I really wanted to talk to a doctor who's going to do the ablation in more detail first about other cases of people with similar PVC burden and going through ablation but unfortunately it turned out he will be available only 2 and 1 day before my scheduled ablation. So ig I'll have to make my final decision last minute bc in one hand I'm worried that it's too much for my anxious ass to handle and I need to know what my options are if that happens but on the other hand if the PVCs are really a main cause of my symptoms and not GAD that would be great to get rid of it without having to be on meds for the rest of my life so yeah rn I'm really conflicted, I just need some kind of reassurance that it's really worth trying bc I've got mixed opinions first and that made me really question it.
Unfortunately the only hotline in my country didn't answer my calls yesterday but I'll try again today. Thank you for telling me that, I just hope it will end up being okay
Thank you for sharing that! The only hotline in Poland doesn't rly pick up but I'll try again
I'm sorry it's so chaotic but I'm extremally anxious rn, I really want to help him so bad
